reason: Re-read in full on 2026-11-15 in the source. The built sidecar dist/spec/evals-baseline/1.0.md and the built dist/spec/evals-baseline/1.0.html, from a build of the working tree (npm run build), were read by script for tables, numbers, dates and digests. Two changes in the reference implementation reached the page. The owner decided on 2026-11-15 to make them in version 1.0 and not in a 1.1, because 1.0 is unpublished and the versioning section lets an unpublished version change. Each passage named below was read against src/printable.mjs, src/compare.mjs, src/render.mjs, src/record.mjs, src/command.mjs and src/quantise.mjs of the implementation and against its regenerated fixtures/vectors.json, which site/src/data/spec/evals-baseline-1.0/vectors.json now copies byte for byte (190 vectors, 914701 bytes, SHA-256 cb64df146452131268140fbc67b1c3074e14572739b548ccf0638fa4d2cfd95c). Passages that the two changes do not touch were re-read and were not checked again against the implementation; their reads of 2026-11-12 stand, and are in the history of this file at commit 8108cbe. Noise fixes: the intro says a sample count has fallen; rule 4 is named 'A smaller sample count fails' and says a larger count is no finding and prints a note; the rule 2 message carries the sample count of the run and of the baseline, and its clause says the message does not say how many cases the drop is; the notes list gained the rise note; the record clauses are now three bullets: keep a held tolerance for a key of the same tool and give any other key --tolerance, refuse when a key has neither, and refuse when --tolerance differs under q from a held tolerance, with a note for each such key in sorted order. The implementation prints how many metrics lack a tolerance and does not name them, so the page says that. The brief for this change expected that refusal to name the keys with their sample counts, and expected a tool name to be listed among the quoted texts; the implementation does neither, because it prints a count and prints a tool name as it is, and the page follows the implementation. Quoting and escaping: the finding form puts the key between double quotes, the rule 3 note quotes each key and separates keys with a comma and a space, and the notes gained the form for a metric that cannot be read and the version note with quoted versions. The first clause of Printed lines was rewritten and not patched: the list of ranges is gone. Text from a file or the command line is printed between double quotes; a character is printed as it is only if it is a space or has General_Category L, M, N, P or S and not Default_Ignorable_Code_Point; every other character is replaced; a left bracket after two number signs is replaced; an escape is four lowercase hexadecimal digits up to U+FFFF and a braced five or six digits above; a surrogate with no partner is one character; quoting does not make text safe to obey. A tool name is one of the two words promptfoo and deepeval, which the baseline reader enforces, so the page says it is printed as it is. The Unicode floor is 15.1. The implementation declares node >= 22, Node.js 22.0.0 reports Unicode 15.1 (measured on that binary), and the 190 vectors reproduce on six Node builds (22.0.0, 22.12.0, 22.22.2, 22.23.5, 24.22.3 and 26.13.1) that carry Unicode 15.1, 16.0, 17.0, 17.0, 17.0 and 18.0. U+1FAE9, which Unicode 16.0 assigns, is replaced under 15.1 and printed as it is under 16.0, and the vectors hold no such character. The baseline-file section says a replaced character is written as the JSON escape of each UTF-16 code unit, and that a left bracket after two number signs is kept. The conformance counts were recomputed from the vectors: 190 vectors (125 check, 34 record, 25 show, 1 version, 5 usage) from 62 pairs, 8 vectors with two findings, 87 with none, 22 silent checks, 65 others, 111 rows and 4 reference-only; the silent-check sentence names a run with more samples. No vector pins a lone surrogate, a private-use code point, a separator other than the space and the line separator, a left bracket after two number signs in a written file, the version note or the ', and n more' tail of the rule 3 note; those were checked only by running the implementation. updatedDate is 2026-11-15; publishDate and the changelog date are unchanged. The guards are site/src/data/spec-printed-forms.site.test.mjs (rewritten), site/src/data/spec-unicode-floor.site.test.mjs (new, split out of it so that each file stays under 300 lines; it holds the Unicode floor and the declared Node.js version), site/src/data/spec-vectors.site.test.mjs and site/src/data/spec-values.site.test.mjs. The two rewritten test files went red together on each of these planted pages, run on 2026-11-15 after the split: a page that keeps the old range list, a page that keeps the ranges beside the new rule, a category dropped from the allow list and one added to it, a page with no Unicode floor, a wrong floor, a wrong runtime named for it, a vectors file with a Unicode 16.0 character, an implementation that declares node >= 24, a finding form without quotes, a rule 2 message without the counts, a rise note without its last clause, and a written-file rule without its bracket sentence. site/content-facts.json lost 21, 165, 116, 57, 67, 49 and 102 and gained 190, 125, 34, 62, 8, 87, 65 and 111.
